abstract: A patient with a history of pelvic radiation therapy for seminoma presented with a prostatic tumor, which appeared predominantly of high signal intensity on T2-weighted magnetic resonance images; low-signal-intensity tissue also extended to the pelvic sidewall. At surgical pathology, the tumor was determined to be radiation-induced sarcoma of the prostate, and the extraprostatic tissue was postradiation fibrosis.
abstract_ja: セミノーマに対する骨盤放射線療法の既往がある患者が、前立腺腫瘍を呈した。T2強調MRIでは主に高信号を示す腫瘍であり、低信号組織は骨盤側壁まで延びていた。外科病理学的検査で、腫瘍は放射線誘発性前立腺肉腫と判定され、前立腺外の組織は放射線後の線維化であった。
